Put a time limit on a request

req_limits.Rd

One limit for the whole request and one for connecting, the connection taking in name resolution and the TLS handshake as libcurl counts it. The order is the point of having it written once: httr2::req_timeout() sets connecttimeout back to 0, which is libcurl's default of 300 seconds, so the connection limit has to come after it. Found on 0.26.0, with the module.

Usage

req_limits(req, limits)

Arguments

req

An httr2 request.

limits

A list with total and connect, in seconds.

Value

The request, with timeout_ms and connecttimeout set.

Details

Every door of the package to a service goes through it: the module (module_call()), the register (register_call()), Graph (directory_page(), directory_create_user()) and the mail service (mail_send()). The values are each door's own, next to it. The one request left out is the reading of the suppressions (suppression_read()), which has had thirty seconds in all since 0.26.0; a total covers the connection too.
